coordinates.locator: Nominatim result for 'Oto Gojo Nara Japan' (way 70543073, Oto Bridge on National Route 168)
coordinates.note: Approximate, campus-grade (precision 6 km): the geocoder's point for the Oto bridge, at the Oto end of the Tentsuji Tunnel region. No official page or paper read gives the observatory's latitude and longitude; the laboratory is about 3 km inside a 5 km tunnel between Oto and Nishiyoshino. It is not a detector or underground-laboratory position.

depth_mwe.note: PICO-LON papers quote about 1200 m.w.e. (arXiv:astro-ph/0611700) and the RCNP group page about 470 m maximum depth; the 2001 annual report of the observatory is followed.
depth_mwe.quote: The maximum depth of the tunnel is about 500 m (1400 m w.e.).

depth_rock.note: Maximum depth of the tunnel; the RCNP group page gives about 470 m.
depth_rock.quote: The maximum depth of the tunnel is about 500 m (1400 m w.e.).

name: Oto Cosmo Observatory (Tentsuji Tunnel)
notes: A17: the coordinate rests on a geocoder (rank 8), so it is a campus-grade point marked approximate and is not relabelled as a detector or underground-laboratory position.

summary.plain: A small underground laboratory in a road tunnel in Nara prefecture, Japan, about 100 km south of Osaka.
summary.technical: RCNP Oto Cosmo Observatory, in the centre of the 5 km Tentsuji Tunnel between Oto and Nishiyoshino; the point recorded is the Oto end of the tunnel region, not the laboratory.
